review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

2:1.sourceText: καὶ ὑμᾶς ὄντας νεκροὺς τοῖς παραπτώμασιν καὶ ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν,
2:1.targetText: Also you—being dead in trespasses and sins,

groups.note: Actual dative article and trespasses noun jointly supply in ... trespasses as the circumstance of dead. The relation remains with the case-bearing nominal head; no independent Greek in preposition is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.
Source-witness possessive difference: N1904 has your, ὑμῶν, after sins; LSV/TR has no separate your there.

2:2.sourceText: ἐν αἷς ποτε περιεπατήσατε κατὰ τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ κόσμου τούτου, κατὰ τὸν ἄρχοντα τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ ἀέρος, τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ νῦν ἐνεργοῦντος ἐν τοῖς υἱοῖς τῆς ἀπειθείας·
2:2.targetText: in which you once walked according to the age of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, of the spirit that is now working in the sons of disobedience,

2:3.sourceText: ἐν οἷς καὶ ἡμεῖς πάντες ἀνεστράφημέν ποτε ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν, ποιοῦντες τὰ θελήματα τῆς σαρκὸς καὶ τῶν διανοιῶν, καὶ ἤμεθα τέκνα φύσει ὀργῆς ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποί·
2:3.targetText: among whom we also all walked once in the desires of our flesh, doing the wishes of the flesh and of the thoughts, and were by nature children of wrath—as also the others,

groups.note: ἀναστρέφομαι here describes ones conduct/manner of life; LSV uses walked figuratively for the same conduct, not a claim that the Greek is the ordinary physical walking verb περιπατέω.

2:4.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Θεὸς πλούσιος ὢν ἐν ἐλέει, διὰ τὴν πολλὴν ἀγάπην αὐτοῦ ἣν ἠγάπησεν ἡμᾶς,
2:4.targetText: but God, being rich in kindness, because of His great love with which He loved us,

groups.note: Greek ἔλεος denotes mercy/compassionate kindness, rendered kindness by LSV. This occurrence retains its actual mercy lemma, distinct from the χρηστότης kindness noun in2:7.
The cognate-object relative ἣν with loved, the love which He loved us, is rendered with which He loved us. With expresses that English cognate-love relation, not a separate Greek preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.
The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

2:5.sourceText: καὶ ὄντας ἡμᾶς νεκροὺς τοῖς παραπτώμασιν συνεζωοποίησεν τῷ Χριστῷ,— χάριτί ἐστε σεσῳσμένοι,—
2:5.targetText: even being dead in the trespasses, made us alive together with the Christ (by grace you are saved),

groups.note: The one Greek ἡμᾶς belongs to the coordinated making-alive, raising and seating actions. It anchors us here and both bracketed [us] objects in LSV2:6, each referring to the same actual original pronoun.
The dative trespasses noun phrase gives the sphere/circumstance of being dead; LSV uses in the for that relation.
The compound συνεζωοποίησεν means made alive together; together is supplied by its συν- prefix, not by an invented separate Greek word.
The instrumental dative χάριτι is rendered by grace as a whole case-marked noun phrase.

2:6.sourceText: καὶ συνήγειρεν καὶ συνεκάθισεν ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ,
2:6.targetText: and raised [us] up together, and sat [us] together in the heavenly [places] in Christ Jesus,

groups.note: The compound συνήγειρεν denotes raised together; LSV expresses its co-action prefix as up together.
The compound συνεκάθισεν denotes seated together; English transitive sat [us] together retains that action and its συν- prefix, not an intransitive sitting of God himself.

Both bracketed [us] objects repeat the actual shared Greek2:5 ἡμᾶς as the object of the coordinated made-alive/raised/seated predicates. That same source word also remains linked to us in2:5; it is a genuine cross-reference one-to-many rendering, not source movement.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English noun completes the substantival heavenly phrase; Greek has no separate places noun.

2:7.sourceText: ἵνα ἐνδείξηται ἐν τοῖς αἰῶσιν τοῖς ἐπερχομένοις τὸ ὑπερβάλλον πλοῦτος τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ ἐν χρηστότητι ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
2:7.targetText: that He might show, in the ages that are coming, the exceeding riches of His grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus,

2:8.sourceText: τῇ γὰρ χάριτί ἐστε σεσῳσμένοι διὰ πίστεως· καὶ τοῦτο οὐκ ἐξ ὑμῶν, Θεοῦ τὸ δῶρον·
2:8.targetText: for by grace you are saved, through faith, and this [is] not of yourselves—[it is] the gift of God,

groups.note: The instrumental dative noun phrase τῇ χάριτι is rendered by grace; the Greek article is absorbed within the English nominal case construction.

The source ὑμῶν is the second-person plural personal pronoun in of you; LSV uses yourselves as the same recipients in the contrast with God as source. No different person or separate Greek reflexive is claimed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.
Bracketed English demonstrative and copula supply the verbless God’s-gift clause; no separate subject pronoun or copula occurs in that Greek clause.

2:9.sourceText: οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων, ἵνα μή τις καυχήσηται.
2:9.targetText: not of works, that no one may boast;

2:10.sourceText: αὐτοῦ γάρ ἐσμεν ποίημα, κτισθέντες ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἐπὶ ἔργοις ἀγαθοῖς, οἷς προητοίμασεν ὁ Θεὸς ἵνα ἐν αὐτοῖς περιπατήσωμεν.
2:10.targetText: for we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus on good works, which God prepared before, that we may walk in them.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

2:11.sourceText: Διὸ μνημονεύετε ὅτι ποτὲ ὑμεῖς τὰ ἔθνη ἐν σαρκί, οἱ λεγόμενοι ἀκροβυστία ὑπὸ τῆς λεγομένης περιτομῆς ἐν σαρκὶ χειροποιήτου,
2:11.targetText: For this reason, remember, that you [were] once the nations in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that called Circumcision in the flesh made by hands,

groups.note: The compound adjective χειροποίητος means made by hands/handmade; the English made and hands render this one word, not separate Greek verb and hand tokens.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

2:12.sourceText: ὅτι ἦτε τῷ καιρῷ ἐκείνῳ χωρὶς Χριστοῦ, ἀπηλλοτριωμένοι τῆς πολιτείας τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ξένοι τῶν διαθηκῶν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας, ἐλπίδα μὴ ἔχοντες καὶ ἄθεοι ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ.
2:12.targetText: that you were at that time apart from Christ, having been alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of the promise, having no hope, and without God in the world;

groups.note: The genitive citizenship phrase complements alienated; English expresses this complement relation as from the commonwealth rather than a separately printed Greek from preposition.
The genitive covenant phrase complements strangers/foreign to; English supplies to the for that complement construction.
The privative compound ἄθεοι means godless/without God; the whole English without God corresponds to that adjective, without inventing a separate source God noun.

2:13.sourceText: νυνὶ δὲ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ὑμεῖς οἵ ποτε ὄντες μακρὰν ἐγενήθητε ἐγγὺς ἐν τῷ αἵματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
2:13.targetText: but now, in Christ Jesus, you being once far off became near in the blood of the Christ,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article/relative οἵ introduces the former-being-far-off participial description; LSV renders it as you being once far off without a separate who or article.

2:14.sourceText: Αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ἡ εἰρήνη ἡμῶν, ὁ ποιήσας τὰ ἀμφότερα ἓν καὶ τὸ μεσότοιχον τοῦ φραγμοῦ λύσας, τὴν ἔχθραν, ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ
2:14.targetText: for He is our peace, who made both one, and broke down the middle wall of the partition of hostility,

groups.note: The aorist loosening/dismantling participle λύσας is rendered by the finite English broke down in the relative who-made construction; the same dismantling event remains linked.

LSV renders the one original Greek2:14 ἔχθραν twice: explanatory of hostility with partition here and the enmity at2:15. Both English realizations refer to this same actual noun identity. The English genitive explanatory modifier is a recasting of the Greek accusative apposition, not a second original hostility noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.
The Greek article in the flesh phrase rendered in LSV2:15 has no separate English article because English uses His flesh; its flesh noun and possessive have actual foreign-source anchors there.

sourceMoved.reason: The article with enmity and the in-His-flesh words from raw Greek2:14 are rendered exclusively in LSV2:15. The actual enmity noun18 is shared between LSV hostility2:14 and enmity2:15 and therefore is not marked moved.

2:15.sourceText: τὸν νόμον τῶν ἐντολῶν ἐν δόγμασιν καταργήσας, ἵνα τοὺς δύο κτίσῃ ἐν αὑτῷ εἰς ἕνα καινὸν ἄνθρωπον ποιῶν εἰρήνην,
2:15.targetText: the enmity in His flesh, having done away [with] the Law of the commands in ordinances, that He might create the two into one new man in Himself, making peace,

groups.note: This enmity phrase belongs to raw Greek2:14. The same noun18 also supplies LSV of hostility in2:14, an explicit explanatory duplication in English; source identity is intentionally shared, not moved or invented.
Pinned N1904 writes the contracted reflexive αὑτῷ (rough breathing), corresponding to Himself. This is distinct from plain αὐτῷ (smooth breathing); the exact source spelling is preserved.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English complement preposition completes done away with; Greek καταργήσας directly governs the Law noun without a separate with preposition.

2:16.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκαταλλάξῃ τοὺς ἀμφοτέρους ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι τῷ Θεῷ διὰ τοῦ σταυροῦ, ἀποκτείνας τὴν ἔχθραν ἐν αὐτῷ·
2:16.targetText: and might reconcile both in one body to God through the Cross, having slain the enmity by it,

groups.note: The dative third-person αὐτῷ can refer to the Cross or to Christ in the context; LSV chooses by it, understood with the Cross. The pair records that English referent interpretation without deciding the alternative in Him reading.

2:17.sourceText: καὶ ἐλθὼν εὐηγγελίσατο εἰρήνην ὑμῖν τοῖς μακρὰν καὶ εἰρήνην τοῖς ἐγγύς·
2:17.targetText: and having come, He proclaimed good news—peace to you—the far-off and the near,

groups.note: N1904 repeats peace with the far-off and the near; LSV has one shared peace governing both coordinated recipient groups (TR also omits the second noun). Both actual Greek peace tokens share that one English counterpart.

2:18.sourceText: ὅτι δι’ αὐτοῦ ἔχομεν τὴν προσαγωγὴν οἱ ἀμφότεροι ἐν ἑνὶ Πνεύματι πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα.
2:18.targetText: because through Him we have the access—we both—in one Spirit to the Father.

groups.note: The substantival nominative οἱ ἀμφότεροι explicitly identifies both of us as the access-having subjects; English renders it we both, retaining the first-person participants already encoded in ἔχομεν.

2:19.sourceText: ἄρα οὖν οὐκέτι ἐστὲ ξένοι καὶ πάροικοι, ἀλλὰ ἐστὲ συνπολῖται τῶν ἁγίων καὶ οἰκεῖοι τοῦ Θεοῦ,
2:19.targetText: Then, therefore, you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but fellow-citizens of the holy ones, and of the household of God,

groups.note: N1904 repeats you are before the contrasted fellow-citizens predicate; LSV shares one you are across no-longer strangers ... but fellow-citizens. Both actual copulas therefore share the one English finite predicate.
The substantival adjective οἰκεῖοι means household members/those belonging to a household; LSV renders this as of the household, not a separate Greek of preposition or house noun.

2:20.sourceText: ἐποικοδομηθέντες ἐπὶ τῷ θεμελίῳ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ προφητῶν, ὄντος ἀκρογωνιαίου αὐτοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ,
2:20.targetText: being built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ Himself being chief corner-[stone],

groups.note: The substantival corner-position adjective ἀκρογωνιαίου is the chief/cornerstone designation. LSV supplies stone in brackets within chief corner-[stone]; the complete architectural designation corresponds to this compound adjective, without an independently printed λίθος noun.

2:21.sourceText: ἐν ᾧ πᾶσα οἰκοδομὴ συναρμολογουμένη αὔξει εἰς ναὸν ἅγιον ἐν Κυρίῳ,
2:21.targetText: in whom all the building fitly framed together increases to a holy temple in the LORD,

review.note: N1904 has anarthrous πᾶσα οἰκοδομή, which can be read every building; LSV all the building follows the TR definite-article reading πᾶσα ἡ οἰκοδομή and a collective whole-building interpretation. Shared building/quantifier lexemes are retained without claiming identical article readings or deciding the interpretive question.

2:22.sourceText: ἐν ᾧ καὶ ὑμεῖς συνοικοδομεῖσθε εἰς κατοικητήριον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν Πνεύματι.
2:22.targetText: in whom you also are built together, for a habitation of God in the Spirit.
